advancements.palimpsest.bleed_through.de: The lower writing is coming through.
advancements.palimpsest.cartographer.des: Read the last of Idris Wray's folios.
advancements.palimpsest.dont_blink.descr: It only moves when you aren't looking. So look.
advancements.palimpsest.dont_blink.title: Don't Blink
advancements.palimpsest.ending_sealed.de: Write your name over the tear.
advancements.palimpsest.ending_unwritten: Scrape your own name off the page.
advancements.palimpsest.gall_iron.title: Iron That Drank Ink
advancements.palimpsest.illuminated.desc: Gold for the capitals. Fire for the ink.
advancements.palimpsest.inkbane.title: Inkbane
Use a Bookmark to come home.
advancements.palimpsest.lower_writing.de: A lullaby from the first draft.
advancements.palimpsest.many_hands.descr: Read a rite with someone at your side.
advancements.palimpsest.many_hands.title: Many Hands
advancements.palimpsest.marginalia.descr: Begin keeping notes. You will need them.
advancements.palimpsest.marginalia.title: Marginalia
advancements.palimpsest.opened_it.title: You Had to Know
advancements.palimpsest.rasure.descripti: Blunt the knife that scraped the first draft.
advancements.palimpsest.rasure.title: Rasure
advancements.palimpsest.read_aloud.title: Read Aloud
advancements.palimpsest.root.description: Something on this page has been written before.
advancements.palimpsest.root.title: Palimpsest
advancements.palimpsest.rubrication.desc: Is this really a good idea?
advancements.palimpsest.spine.title: Spine
advancements.palimpsest.station_four.des: Their logs stop on the same day.
advancements.palimpsest.the_bindery.desc: A building sewn together with red thread.
advancements.palimpsest.the_desk.descrip: Every copy begins at a desk.
advancements.palimpsest.the_desk.title: A Steady Hand
advancements.palimpsest.the_hand.title: The Hand
advancements.palimpsest.the_rubricator.d: Meet the scribe whose headings survived.
advancements.palimpsest.the_tear.title: The Tear
advancements.palimpsest.the_undertext.de: The lower writing. The first draft.
advancements.palimpsest.three_knocks.des: Don't open it. It leaves at dawn.
advancements.palimpsest.under_the_surfac: Scratch the surface and it scratches back.
advancements.palimpsest.vermilion.descri: Red ink does not scrape away.
advancements.palimpsest.vermilion.title: Vermilion
advancements.palimpsest.warded.title: Red at the Threshold
advancements.palimpsest.which_one.title: Which One of You
advancements.palimpsest.written_twice.de: The second writing didn't quite cover the first.
codex.palimpsest.bindery.text: A building made of books, sewn together with red thread. The Bookbinder waits inside. The Margin Compass points here in the lower page.
codex.palimpsest.bindery.title: The Bindery
codex.palimpsest.blotling.text: A drop of ink that decided to move. Splits when struck. A rasorium makes short work of them; so does keeping your feet dry.
codex.palimpsest.blotling.title: Blotling
codex.palimpsest.bookbinder.text: Idris Wray tried to sew the tear shut from the inside and the Bindery sewed him into itself: a hunched man grown into a heap of stitched books, walking on needles. At half strength it rebinds itself through three stitched tomes; break them and it falls open. It was a cartographer, once.
codex.palimpsest.bookbinder.title: The Bookbinder
codex.palimpsest.bookmark.text: Keeps your place. Used above, it remembers where you stand; used below, it takes you back there, and is spent.
codex.palimpsest.bookmark.title: Bookmark
codex.palimpsest.broken_gate.text: A red-framed doorway deep underground, cracked through. Somebody tried to read their way down, a long time ago, and the reading failed.
codex.palimpsest.broken_gate.title: Broken Gate
codex.palimpsest.copying_house.text: A ruined scriptorium in the dark woods. Desks, ink, vellum, and a great deal of work abandoned mid-sentence.
codex.palimpsest.copying_house.title: The Copying House
codex.palimpsest.copyist.text: Something that learned what an animal is by watching them, and got it almost right. It wears a cow or a pig or a sheep and stands with the herd. Tells: no shadow, never grazes, always facing me, a voice a little too low. Up close, fed, struck or seen through a Reading Lens, it stops pretending.
codex.palimpsest.copyist.title: The Copyist
codex.palimpsest.crow_roost.text: A dead tree hung with black feathers. The quillcrows sleep here, facing outward.
codex.palimpsest.crow_roost.title: Crow Roost
codex.palimpsest.doubled_house.text: A house that exists twice, one inside the other: a door that opens onto a wall, stairs that meet the ceiling. The second writing did not quite cover the first.
codex.palimpsest.doubled_house.title: The House Written Twice
codex.palimpsest.erratum.text: A block that is in the wrong place. I stood on it. When I looked back it was closer.
codex.palimpsest.erratum.title: Erratum
codex.palimpsest.faded_pages.text: Pages from the first draft, most of their words scraped to noise. The faded people drop them. The Rubricator collects them.
codex.palimpsest.faded_pages.title: Faded Pages
codex.palimpsest.faded_village.text: Outlines of houses and the faded people who still keep them. The Rubricator is often here.
codex.palimpsest.faded_village.title: Faded Village
codex.palimpsest.fading.text: Grass going grey in patches, as if the colour had been rubbed out. It grows back in sunlight, slowly. It is worse near where I sleep.
codex.palimpsest.fading.title: Fading
codex.palimpsest.fair_copy.text: In a manuscript the fair copy is the clean final version, made from the messy draft. I saw myself, holding what I held, standing where I was not. It walked away when I came near. I did not strike it. Wray's note says: do not touch yourself.
codex.palimpsest.fair_copy.title: The Fair Copy
codex.palimpsest.fog.text: A fog came in from nowhere and stayed exactly as long as I was frightened of it.
codex.palimpsest.fog.title: Fog
codex.palimpsest.folio_1.text:
The survey of the northern reach is complete, save for one hill I cannot account for.

I drew it on the Tuesday: a round green hill with a single oak on its shoulder. On the Thursday it was gone. Where it had stood the grass was pale and flat, as if something had been rubbed out with the heel of a hand, and the oak lay on its side with no stump.

I have redrawn the sheet. I will not mention this to the Society.

- I. Wray
codex.palimpsest.folio_1.title: Folio I: The Northern Reach
codex.palimpsest.folio_10.text:
There is something tall down here that only moves when I look away.

In the dark I cannot tell whether I am looking at it or not, and neither, I think, can it. Carry a light.

My knife went through it like smoke. The red scribe says the gold the old illuminators laid on their capitals, illumine, burns it; so does iron that has drunk gall-ink. He says it will not cross red chalk, and will not stand near a lit ward.

I am making a sword. I am also going to stop looking behind me.
codex.palimpsest.folio_10.title: Folio X: The Tall One
codex.palimpsest.folio_11.text:
Tonight I heard it: a long scraping, far off, the sound a knife makes on vellum. Moving.

The red scribe says it is the Rasure: the knife that scraped the first draft, left behind when the writer moved on to the new page. It is still working. It does not know it is finished. It is working its way up.

There is a place where the tear between the pages is widest, where the last page of the first draft is kept. The Bindery guards the way to it.

I am going to sew the tear shut from this side. If this is my last folio, the compass will show you the Bindery. Bring red.
codex.palimpsest.folio_11.title: Folio XI: The Rasure
codex.palimpsest.folio_12.text:
The thread holds. The needles hold. I hold.

I can feel the books growing into my back. The spine of them is my spine. I think I have been here a very long time.

If you are reading this you have cut me loose, and I am grateful, and I am sorry.

The key is my spine: take it. The Last Folio lies past the stitched door. Bind your compass to it at the altar. When you face the Rasure, re-ink the pillars; it cannot abide the red. When the page goes white, listen for footsteps.

And when it is done you will be given a choice. I do not know the right one. I only know what I would have chosen, and I cannot remember what it was.
codex.palimpsest.folio_12.title: Folio XII: The Bookbinder
codex.palimpsest.folio_2.text:
The masons call it palimpsest stone: the grey that shows letters when it is wet.

This morning I took a penknife to a vein of it, the way a scribe scrapes old vellum clean to use it again. A rasorium, they called the knife in the scriptoria. The surface came away in a curl, like wax.

Underneath there was writing. Not carving. Writing, in an ink that was still wet.

The flake I lifted is on my desk. It is warm.
codex.palimpsest.folio_2.title: Folio II: On the Grey Stone
codex.palimpsest.folio_3.text:
The lower writing will only take iron-gall ink. Soot ink smears off it like breath off glass.

The old recipe: oak galls (the little brown nuts wasps leave on oak leaves; knock enough leaves down and you will find them), a nail's worth of iron, and a clean bottle. Let it blacken.

I keep a commonplace book now, as scholars used to: everything I notice, written down the day I notice it. A book, a gall for the ink, a feather to write with. I recommend it. Some days the book seems to know things before I write them.
codex.palimpsest.folio_3.title: Folio III: Gall and Iron
codex.palimpsest.folio_4.text:
Something knocked at the cabin door at the third hour.

Three knocks. A pause long enough to breathe in. Three more.

I did not answer. At dawn there were no prints in the frost, only a long pale streak down the outside of the door, as if someone very tall had leaned the whole length of themselves against it and waited.

I have learned this much: whatever knocks after midnight is not asking to be let in. It is asking you to open the door.
codex.palimpsest.folio_4.title: Folio IV: The Knocking
codex.palimpsest.folio_5.text:
The rubricators, the monks who wrote the red headings in old books, used vermilion, which is ground cinnabar. Cinnabar lies deep, where the stone is hot.

It is a mineral. It does not soak into the page; it sits on it. I think that is why, wherever the lower writing shows, the red letters have survived and the black have not.

I drew a red line across my threshold in chalk made from it. The knocking stopped. I have not slept better in a year.
codex.palimpsest.folio_5.title: Folio V: Vermilion
codex.palimpsest.folio_6.text:
Copying is not enough. The old writers had a way of making a page do something. They called it rubrication.

A red altar at the centre. Stands around it, close, each holding one piece of the sentence. You hold the last word yourself, and read it at the altar.

Some sentences only read at night. Some only under a new moon, or in a storm, or in the lower page itself. Every sentence costs you something to read. And some sentences, read wrong, read back.
codex.palimpsest.folio_6.title: Folio VI: Rubrication
codex.palimpsest.folio_7.text:
The stone says this world was written over another.

Same hills. Same rivers. Same sea. The same seed, grown twice. The first draft was scraped away to make room for this one, as a scribe scrapes a page he means to reuse.

It was not scraped well. The people of the first draft are still there underneath, thin as breath, going about their days in a world with half its words gone. They call their place the Undertext.

They can see us. We are the upper writing. We are written on top of them.
codex.palimpsest.folio_7.title: Folio VII: The First Draft
codex.palimpsest.folio_8.text:
A door into the lower page must be framed in red: rubricated vellum, the opening two wide and three high.

The Folio of Descent is written at the altar, at night, above ground: four fragments of the lower writing, a sheet of blank vellum, iron-gall ink, a black quill, and a candlewort flower, read over a book. Read the Folio aloud at the frame, after dark.

I have made one. The lamps went out when I finished writing it, all of them at once.

I have not used it yet.
codex.palimpsest.folio_8.title: Folio VIII: The Door
codex.palimpsest.folio_9.text:
I went down.

The sky is the colour of old paper and lit from nowhere. There is a black sun that does not move. It is quiet the way a page is quiet.

The faded people walk the same few steps again and again, as if re-reading a line they cannot finish. If you watch one long enough, it notices. It follows. It means no harm.

One of them spoke: a scribe in red, whose name had been scraped away but whose headings had not. He trades. He wants the pages that fall from the faded ones, and the fragments of lower writing, and he gives what he kept. A bookmark from him brought me home.
codex.palimpsest.folio_9.title: Folio IX: Below
codex.palimpsest.folio_gate.text: Frame a doorway in rubricated vellum bricks: the opening two wide, three high. Read a Folio of Descent at the frame, at night. Stand in the veil until it finishes the sentence. The Undertext lies directly beneath: the gate below opens where the gate above stands.
codex.palimpsest.folio_gate.title: Folio Gates
codex.palimpsest.footsteps.text: Footsteps behind me, unhurried, stopping when I stop. Once, sounds I know: a chest lid, a hiss, a door. Nothing there when I turn. It is always behind me.
codex.palimpsest.footsteps.title: Footsteps
codex.palimpsest.foxing_moth.text: Pale moths freckled brown like old paper. They drift toward light and leave a fine dust. Harmless. Where there are many of them, the page is thin.
codex.palimpsest.foxing_moth.title: Foxing Moth
codex.palimpsest.gall_iron.text: Iron steeped in iron-gall ink, then blasted: it holds an edge against ink. Inkbane.
codex.palimpsest.gall_iron.title: Gall Iron
codex.palimpsest.hollow_chapel.text: A chapel with a red altar where the font should be, and hymnals with every hymn scraped out except the headings.
codex.palimpsest.hollow_chapel.title: Hollow Chapel
codex.palimpsest.illumine.text: Gilt from the lower page: the gold leaf illuminators laid on their capitals. It glows. It burns ink.
codex.palimpsest.illumine.title: Illumine
codex.palimpsest.ink_rain.text: It rained, and the rain was black, and it did not wet anything.
codex.palimpsest.ink_rain.title: Ink Rain
codex.palimpsest.ink_well.text: A great round shaft of inkstone going down into the black. Hounds circle it. There is gilt at the bottom.
codex.palimpsest.ink_well.title: Ink Well
codex.palimpsest.inkhound.text: Lean hounds of dried ink with no eyes. They hunt by sound: sprinting, jumping, fighting, digging. Crouch, move slowly, and they lose you.
codex.palimpsest.inkhound.title: Inkhound
codex.palimpsest.iron_gall_ink.text: Oak galls, iron, a bottle. The only ink the lower writing takes. Oak galls fall from oak leaves.
codex.palimpsest.iron_gall_ink.title: Iron-Gall Ink
codex.palimpsest.knocker.text: Taller than a door, arms to its knees. It comes to houses at night and knocks: three, and three. It cannot open doors. It waits for you to. If you do, or if you step outside while it is there, it comes for you, fast. Light and red wards drive it off. At dawn it leaves.
codex.palimpsest.knocker.title: The Knocker
codex.palimpsest.knocking.text: Three knocks at the door after dark. A pause. Three more. I did not open it. Wray says: it is not asking to come in. It is asking you to open the door.
codex.palimpsest.knocking.title: Knocking
codex.palimpsest.last_folio.text: Past the stitched door: four pillars, an altar, and the last page of the first draft. Read the Rite of the Last Reading here and the Rasure comes.
codex.palimpsest.last_folio.title: The Last Folio
codex.palimpsest.longhand.text: One long pen-stroke of a figure. It only moves when no one is looking, and in darkness no one is. Ordinary weapons pass through it. Inkbane cuts. It will not cross red chalk or come near a lit ward. At dawn it is gone. Carry light. Do not blink.
codex.palimpsest.longhand.title: The Longhand
codex.palimpsest.margin_compass.text: Points at the nearest place where the page is thin. Above: old ruins. Below: the Bindery. Bound at the altar with the Bookbinder's needle, it points to the Last Folio.
codex.palimpsest.margin_compass.title: Margin Compass
codex.palimpsest.margin_crawler.text: The doodles from the margins of old manuscripts: a snail in a knight's helmet, a lance too long for it. They climb walls and go for the ankles. Silly, until there are six.
codex.palimpsest.margin_crawler.title: Margin Crawler
codex.palimpsest.marginalia_spire.text: A tower drawn in the margin by someone bored: too tall, too thin, full of doodles that crawl.
codex.palimpsest.marginalia_spire.title: Marginalia Spire
codex.palimpsest.moved_things.text: A door I shut is open. A chest I packed is in a different order: everything there, nothing where it was. Things are being read, and put back carelessly.
codex.palimpsest.moved_things.title: Moved Things
codex.palimpsest.pale_stag.text: A deer the colour of blank paper, with no face at all. In the Undertext they graze and bolt. Above, one stands at the treeline, facing me, and is gone before I can get near.
codex.palimpsest.pale_stag.title: Pale Stag
codex.palimpsest.palehand.text: Far away, at night, behind the hills: a hand the size of a mountain, pale as bone, moving its fingers as if writing. Then it went back down. I do not think it knew I was there. I do not think it knows anything is there.
codex.palimpsest.palehand.title: The Hand
codex.palimpsest.palimpsest_stone.text: Grey stone with older writing just beneath the surface. Mined, it is just stone. Scraped with a rasorium, it gives up a fragment of the lower writing and turns pale.
codex.palimpsest.palimpsest_stone.title: Palimpsest Stone
codex.palimpsest.quillcrow.text: Crows with steel nibs for beaks. Watchers. They sit high and take their leave when approached. Killing one is remembered, and not by me.
codex.palimpsest.quillcrow.title: Quillcrow
codex.palimpsest.rasorium.text: A scribe's scraping knife. Scrapes palimpsest stone, vellum soil and signs (you learn what they said before). Quick in a fight, and bites deep into anything made of ink.
codex.palimpsest.rasorium.title: The Rasorium
codex.palimpsest.rasure.text: The knife that scraped the first draft, still scraping. It lines the floor in red and hollows it. It blanks the four pillars and hides behind their silence: re-ink them with vermilion or chalk. At the end the page goes white and it goes invisible; censer smoke and ink show it, and it has footsteps.
codex.palimpsest.rasure.title: The Rasure
codex.palimpsest.reading_lens.text: Gilt lens with lower writing in the glass. Shows what is made of ink, and what is pretending not to be.
codex.palimpsest.reading_lens.title: Reading Lens
codex.palimpsest.redacted.text: A figure censored with black bars. Its cuts do not heal while Erasure lasts, and sometimes the name of something I carry goes black. Struck, it is somewhere else. Sealing wax stops the Erasure.
codex.palimpsest.redacted.title: The Redacted
codex.palimpsest.remedies.text: Candlewort tea settles the Bleed a little, once in a while. Sealing wax, chewed, stops Erasure and clears ink from the eyes.
codex.palimpsest.remedies.title: Remedies
codex.palimpsest.rites.text:
A Rubric Altar with Reading Stands close around it. Lay one offering on each stand, hold the catalyst, use the altar. Conditions matter: time, moon, weather, which page you stand on. Every rite costs a little of you. Some bite back; friends standing near make that less likely.

Known rites: Warding, the Open Page, Recall, Closing, Unmaking, Quieting, Illumination, Binding, the Last Reading. Others are hinted at.
codex.palimpsest.rites.title: Rites
codex.palimpsest.rubric_chalk.text: Red chalk lines on the ground. To anything made of ink they are a wall. To everything else they are chalk.
codex.palimpsest.rubric_chalk.title: Rubric Chalk
codex.palimpsest.rubric_ward.text: A lamp glazed in vermilion. Inkborn will not come within sixteen blocks. Knockers leave warded doors alone. Tears will not open near it. Sleeping beside one lets the page settle.
codex.palimpsest.rubric_ward.title: Rubric Ward
codex.palimpsest.rubricator.text: The last scribe of the first draft. His name was scraped away; his red headings were not, and neither was he, mostly. He trades what he kept for what I find: faded pages, fragments, gilt. Do not hurt him.
codex.palimpsest.rubricator.title: The Rubricator
codex.palimpsest.scraped_obelisk.text: Standing stones with their faces scraped smooth. Someone wanted something forgotten. Palimpsest stone around the base.
codex.palimpsest.scraped_obelisk.title: Scraped Obelisk
codex.palimpsest.scraping.text: A long scraping sound, and then a stripe of the world is simply blank: white, humming, gone. It comes back after a while. The Rasure is practising.
codex.palimpsest.scraping.title: Scraping
codex.palimpsest.scriptorium_desk.text: A surface, an ink and a subject, worked into something new: compasses, dowsing quills, vestments, and one strange record.
codex.palimpsest.scriptorium_desk.title: Scriptorium Desk
codex.palimpsest.seals.text: Red wax pressed over a rip in the page. Closes a Tear. Writes a blank back at once.
codex.palimpsest.seals.title: Seals of Closing
codex.palimpsest.silence.text: Every sound stopped. Wind, animals, my own footsteps. It lasted about as long as I could hold my breath, and then something snapped, very close.
codex.palimpsest.silence.title: Silence
codex.palimpsest.smudge.text: One of the faded people of the first draft: an outline with the face rubbed out. It walks the same few steps over and over. Look at it long enough and it follows, murmuring. It will not hurt you. Hurt it and it comes apart, sometimes leaving a page.
codex.palimpsest.smudge.title: Smudge
codex.palimpsest.snuffed_torch.text: Torches going out on their own. Not blown out: finished, as if they had burned for a week. Flint and steel lights them again. I have started carrying a lot of flint.
codex.palimpsest.snuffed_torch.title: Spent Torches
codex.palimpsest.someone_typed.text: Words in the chat that nobody wrote. Sometimes in my own name. I have started keeping logs.
codex.palimpsest.someone_typed.title: Someone Typed
codex.palimpsest.stage.1: Something on this page has been written before.
codex.palimpsest.stage.2: The lower writing shows at the edges.
codex.palimpsest.stage.3: The lower writing is coming through.
codex.palimpsest.stage_1.text: I have the sense, lately, of having read this page before. Nothing I can point to. A sound that stopped as I turned. A light that was on and then was not.
codex.palimpsest.stage_1.title: Faint Trace
codex.palimpsest.stage_2.text: Something is written underneath. I catch it at the edges: knocking where no one is, a sign that said one thing and then another, my own things not quite where I left them.
codex.palimpsest.stage_2.title: Ghosting
codex.palimpsest.stage_3.text: The lower writing is coming through. Things stand at the edge of sight and are gone. The fog comes in when it should not. I am no longer sure what is an animal.
codex.palimpsest.stage_3.title: Bleed-through
codex.palimpsest.stage_4.text: The ink is running. The grass fades where I walk. The lights fail together. Sometimes it rains black. Sometimes the world goes silent all at once, as if listening.
codex.palimpsest.stage_4.title: Running Ink
codex.palimpsest.stage_5.text: The page is tearing. There are rips in the air that leak the lower world. Once, for a moment, the sky was the colour of old paper.
codex.palimpsest.stage_5.title: The Tear
codex.palimpsest.stage_6.text: I am being written over. I have seen myself standing where I was not. Something is scraping the ground near my house, and it is careful, and it is patient.
codex.palimpsest.stage_6.title: Overwritten
codex.palimpsest.survey_station.text: An underground survey station: iron doors, logbooks, a gate frame bricked up from the inside. The Anomalous Terrain Survey came looking for Wray. Their logs stop on the same day.
codex.palimpsest.survey_station.title: Station Four
codex.palimpsest.tears.text: Rips in the air, a little taller than me, oozing ink. Things come out of them. A Seal of Closing presses them shut. Wards keep new ones from opening near home.
codex.palimpsest.tears.title: Tears
codex.palimpsest.the_choice.text: The Last Folio lies on its stand, with my name on it. I can write my name over the tear, and the page will be clean. I can read it aloud, and the first draft will stay open around me. There may be a third way. I would need the knife to find it.
codex.palimpsest.the_choice.title: The Choice
codex.palimpsest.the_other_page.text: For a moment, everything around me was the wrong material: pale, ruled with faint lines, the trees black as blots. Then it was the world again. I have not told anyone.
codex.palimpsest.the_other_page.title: The Other Page
codex.palimpsest.the_sign.text: A sign I made said something else when I passed it. When I came back it said what I wrote. I have stopped reading my signs twice.
codex.palimpsest.the_sign.title: The Sign
codex.palimpsest.undertext.text: The lower writing. The first draft. A world like ours with half its words scraped off: paper sky, black sun, ink seas, ruled ground. The bed will not let me sleep. A bookmark will take me home.
codex.palimpsest.undertext.title: The Undertext
codex.palimpsest.vermilion.text: Ground cinnabar: the red of the rubricators, which does not scrape away. Makes rubric chalk, wards, and the red frames of gates. Cinnabar lies deep, near lava.
codex.palimpsest.vermilion.title: Vermilion
codex.palimpsest.watchers.text: Black birds with steel nibs for beaks sit high and watch me, and leave the moment I come near. I killed one. It felt like being noticed. It felt like something wrote that down.
codex.palimpsest.watchers.title: Watchers
codex.palimpsest.whispers.text: Something said something at my ear. Not words, quite. The sound words make before they are finished.
codex.palimpsest.whispers.title: Whispers
codex.palimpsest.wray_cabin.text: A cartographer's cabin, long empty. Maps that do not match the land. A cellar with writing on the walls.
codex.palimpsest.wray_cabin.title: Wray's Cabin
item.palimpsest.black_quill.desc: A quillcrow's feather. Cut to a nib, it writes on the lower page.
item.palimpsest.blank_vellum.desc: Scraped clean, ready to be written on. Something was on it before.
item.palimpsest.blot_residue.desc: What is left of a blotling. Stains everything.
item.palimpsest.blotberry_tart.desc: Stains the teeth for a day.
item.palimpsest.bookbinder_needle.desc: Long enough to sew a building shut.
item.palimpsest.bookmark.use: Above: mark your place. Below: return to it.
item.palimpsest.cinnabar.desc: Heavy red crystal from deep, hot stone.
item.palimpsest.circlet_of_the_first_dra: You see in the dark. The dark sees you too.
item.palimpsest.commonplace_book.desc: Your notes. They seem to write themselves.
item.palimpsest.commonplace_book.use: Use to read. [J] also opens it.
item.palimpsest.dowsing_quill.desc: It twitches toward the lower writing.
item.palimpsest.dowsing_quill.use: Hold to feel for palimpsest stone, gates and tears.
item.palimpsest.faded_page.desc: A page from the first draft. Most of the words are gone.
item.palimpsest.folio_of_descent.desc: Read aloud at a red frame, after dark.
item.palimpsest.folio_of_descent.use: Use on a complete Folio Gate frame at night.
item.palimpsest.foxed_dust.desc: The brown freckles of old paper, shaken off a moth.
item.palimpsest.gall_iron_ingot.desc: Iron that has drunk ink. It remembers how to cut it.
item.palimpsest.illumine_leaf.desc: Gold leaf for the capitals. It gives off a little light, and ink hates it.
item.palimpsest.illumined_censer.desc: Its smoke is light made thick.
item.palimpsest.illumined_censer.use: Use to swing: scalds inkborn, reveals the hidden.
item.palimpsest.ink_bomb.desc: Blinds what it splashes. Shows what hides.
item.palimpsest.iron_gall_ink.desc: The only ink the lower writing will take.
item.palimpsest.iron_rasorium.use: Use on palimpsest stone, vellum or signs to scrape them.
item.palimpsest.last_folio.desc: The last page of the first draft. Your name is on it.
item.palimpsest.last_folio.use: Lay it on the Folio Stand.
item.palimpsest.margin_compass.desc: It points where the page is thin.
item.palimpsest.oak_gall.desc: A wasp's nest in an oak leaf. The black of iron-gall ink.
item.palimpsest.rasure_edge.desc: Forged from the knife that scraped the first draft.
item.palimpsest.rasure_edge.use: Use to erase a creature from the page. Long cooldown.
item.palimpsest.rasure_shard.desc: A sliver of the knife. It is still sharp on every side.
item.palimpsest.raw_illumine.desc: Gilt from the lower page, dull until it is heated.
item.palimpsest.reading_lens.desc: There is lower writing ground into the glass.
item.palimpsest.reading_lens.use: Use to reveal inkborn and read what the stone says.
item.palimpsest.redaction_strip.desc: A bar of pure black, cut from a Redacted. Nothing shows through it.
item.palimpsest.rubric_armor.desc: Inked with rubrics: each piece slows the Bleed by a tenth.
item.palimpsest.rubric_chalk.desc: Draws lines that ink cannot cross.
item.palimpsest.rubric_chalk.use: Use on the ground to draw a line.
item.palimpsest.scribes_ration.desc: Bread and meat wrapped in vellum, for long copying.
item.palimpsest.scriveners_quill.desc: The pen that wrote this world. It still works, for small things.
item.palimpsest.scriveners_quill.use: Use at night to write the morning; in rain, to write it clear.
item.palimpsest.seal_of_closing.desc: Red wax for a torn page.
item.palimpsest.seal_of_closing.use: Use on a Tear or a Blank.
item.palimpsest.sealing_wax.desc: Chewed, it stops Erasure. Tastes of candles.
item.palimpsest.spine_key.desc: Unpicks the stitched door. It is warm, and it has vertebrae.
item.palimpsest.torn_folio.desc: In a cartographer's neat, worried hand.
item.palimpsest.undertext_fragment.desc: A flake of the lower writing, still wet. Warm to the touch.
item.palimpsest.vellum_scrap.desc: A curl of scraped page. Four make a sheet.
item.palimpsest.vermilion.desc: The rubricators' red. It sits on the page and does not scrape.
lore.palimpsest.faded.1.text:
hush now, the page is turning
hush now, the §kink§r is dry

and left the §klamp§r to burn us by

lore.palimpsest.faded.1.title: A Lullaby
lore.palimpsest.faded.10.text:
when the knife comes it is quiet.

you do not hear it. you hear the silence where the birds were.

then you see the red lines on the ground, and you have the time it takes to say your own name to step off them.

say it quickly.
lore.palimpsest.faded.10.title: When It Comes
lore.palimpsest.faded.2.text:
Three cups of §kflour§r, a spoon of salt, warm water.
Knead until it stops being §kstick§r.
Leave it by the §kstove§r under a cloth until it has grown to twice its §k......§r.

We have not had §kbread§r since the east side was scraped. I write it down so that someone remembers the §ksmell§r.
lore.palimpsest.faded.2.title: A Recipe
lore.palimpsest.faded.3.text:
§kAldous Pell§r
§kMarit Pell§r
§kthe Harrow children§r
§kOld Tamsin§r
§kFen§r
§kthe miller§r
§k......§r

We write the names on the red page now. The red page does not scrape.
lore.palimpsest.faded.3.title: A List of Names
lore.palimpsest.faded.4.text:
we are still here

we are still here

we are §kstill§r here

we are §k.....§r here
lore.palimpsest.faded.4.title: Four Words
lore.palimpsest.faded.5.text:
My love,
they are scraping the east side of the village today. You can hear it from the well: a long sound, like someone drawing a breath that does not end. When it passes, the houses are still there but they are §kpale§r, and nobody in them remembers their own §kname§r.

If it comes for our street, do not stand in the road. Stand on the red step. Hold on to something red.

I will meet you at the §k......§r.
lore.palimpsest.faded.5.title: A Letter
lore.palimpsest.faded.6.text:
(The page is a child's drawing: a house with a door, a round sun, four figures holding hands.)

i drew a house so we would have somewhere to live when it comes

(Something has scraped the sun out, very carefully, leaving the rays.)
lore.palimpsest.faded.6.title: A Drawing
lore.palimpsest.faded.7.text:
RULES FOR AFTER DARK
1. Do not open for knocking. Your family has keys.
2. Do not look at the tall one. Do not look away from it either. Carry a lamp.
3. Count your animals twice.
4. If you meet yourself, do not touch yourself.
5. If the birds go quiet, get off the road.
6. §k.............................§r
lore.palimpsest.faded.7.title: Rules
lore.palimpsest.faded.8.text:
the writer did not hate us.

the writer simply finished, and turned the page, and began again.

that is what we cannot forgive.
lore.palimpsest.faded.8.title: A Thought
lore.palimpsest.faded.9.text:
From the well walk toward the black sun until the ground turns red. Where the red is widest there is a building of books, and past it a door sewn shut, and past that the §klast page§r.

The man who went in to sew it closed did not come back out. We hear his needles at night.
lore.palimpsest.faded.9.title: Directions
lore.palimpsest.folio.1.text:
The survey of the northern reach is complete, save for one hill I cannot account for.

I drew it on the Tuesday: a round green hill with a single oak on its shoulder. On the Thursday it was gone. Where it had stood the grass was pale and flat, as if something had been rubbed out with the heel of a hand, and the oak lay on its side with no stump.

I have redrawn the sheet. I will not mention this to the Society.

- I. Wray
lore.palimpsest.folio.1.title: Folio I: The Northern Reach
lore.palimpsest.folio.10.text:
There is something tall down here that only moves when I look away.

In the dark I cannot tell whether I am looking at it or not, and neither, I think, can it. Carry a light.

My knife went through it like smoke. The red scribe says the gold the old illuminators laid on their capitals, illumine, burns it; so does iron that has drunk gall-ink. He says it will not cross red chalk, and will not stand near a lit ward.

I am making a sword. I am also going to stop looking behind me.
lore.palimpsest.folio.10.title: Folio X: The Tall One
lore.palimpsest.folio.11.text:
Tonight I heard it: a long scraping, far off, the sound a knife makes on vellum. Moving.

The red scribe says it is the Rasure: the knife that scraped the first draft, left behind when the writer moved on to the new page. It is still working. It does not know it is finished. It is working its way up.

There is a place where the tear between the pages is widest, where the last page of the first draft is kept. The Bindery guards the way to it.

I am going to sew the tear shut from this side. If this is my last folio, the compass will show you the Bindery. Bring red.
lore.palimpsest.folio.11.title: Folio XI: The Rasure
lore.palimpsest.folio.12.text:
The thread holds. The needles hold. I hold.

I can feel the books growing into my back. The spine of them is my spine. I think I have been here a very long time.

If you are reading this you have cut me loose, and I am grateful, and I am sorry.

The key is my spine: take it. The Last Folio lies past the stitched door. Bind your compass to it at the altar. When you face the Rasure, re-ink the pillars; it cannot abide the red. When the page goes white, listen for footsteps.

And when it is done you will be given a choice. I do not know the right one. I only know what I would have chosen, and I cannot remember what it was.
lore.palimpsest.folio.12.title: Folio XII: The Bookbinder
lore.palimpsest.folio.2.text:
The masons call it palimpsest stone: the grey that shows letters when it is wet.

This morning I took a penknife to a vein of it, the way a scribe scrapes old vellum clean to use it again. A rasorium, they called the knife in the scriptoria. The surface came away in a curl, like wax.

Underneath there was writing. Not carving. Writing, in an ink that was still wet.

The flake I lifted is on my desk. It is warm.
lore.palimpsest.folio.2.title: Folio II: On the Grey Stone
lore.palimpsest.folio.3.text:
The lower writing will only take iron-gall ink. Soot ink smears off it like breath off glass.

The old recipe: oak galls (the little brown nuts wasps leave on oak leaves; knock enough leaves down and you will find them), a nail's worth of iron, and a clean bottle. Let it blacken.

I keep a commonplace book now, as scholars used to: everything I notice, written down the day I notice it. A book, a gall for the ink, a feather to write with. I recommend it. Some days the book seems to know things before I write them.
lore.palimpsest.folio.3.title: Folio III: Gall and Iron
lore.palimpsest.folio.4.text:
Something knocked at the cabin door at the third hour.

Three knocks. A pause long enough to breathe in. Three more.

I did not answer. At dawn there were no prints in the frost, only a long pale streak down the outside of the door, as if someone very tall had leaned the whole length of themselves against it and waited.

I have learned this much: whatever knocks after midnight is not asking to be let in. It is asking you to open the door.
lore.palimpsest.folio.4.title: Folio IV: The Knocking
lore.palimpsest.folio.5.text:
The rubricators, the monks who wrote the red headings in old books, used vermilion, which is ground cinnabar. Cinnabar lies deep, where the stone is hot.

It is a mineral. It does not soak into the page; it sits on it. I think that is why, wherever the lower writing shows, the red letters have survived and the black have not.

I drew a red line across my threshold in chalk made from it. The knocking stopped. I have not slept better in a year.
lore.palimpsest.folio.5.title: Folio V: Vermilion
lore.palimpsest.folio.6.text:
Copying is not enough. The old writers had a way of making a page do something. They called it rubrication.

A red altar at the centre. Stands around it, close, each holding one piece of the sentence. You hold the last word yourself, and read it at the altar.

Some sentences only read at night. Some only under a new moon, or in a storm, or in the lower page itself. Every sentence costs you something to read. And some sentences, read wrong, read back.
lore.palimpsest.folio.6.title: Folio VI: Rubrication
lore.palimpsest.folio.7.text:
The stone says this world was written over another.

Same hills. Same rivers. Same sea. The same seed, grown twice. The first draft was scraped away to make room for this one, as a scribe scrapes a page he means to reuse.

It was not scraped well. The people of the first draft are still there underneath, thin as breath, going about their days in a world with half its words gone. They call their place the Undertext.

They can see us. We are the upper writing. We are written on top of them.
lore.palimpsest.folio.7.title: Folio VII: The First Draft
lore.palimpsest.folio.8.text:
A door into the lower page must be framed in red: rubricated vellum, the opening two wide and three high.

The Folio of Descent is written at the altar, at night, above ground: four fragments of the lower writing, a sheet of blank vellum, iron-gall ink, a black quill, and a candlewort flower, read over a book. Read the Folio aloud at the frame, after dark.

I have made one. The lamps went out when I finished writing it, all of them at once.

I have not used it yet.
lore.palimpsest.folio.8.title: Folio VIII: The Door
lore.palimpsest.folio.9.text:
I went down.

The sky is the colour of old paper and lit from nowhere. There is a black sun that does not move. It is quiet the way a page is quiet.

The faded people walk the same few steps again and again, as if re-reading a line they cannot finish. If you watch one long enough, it notices. It follows. It means no harm.

One of them spoke: a scribe in red, whose name had been scraped away but whose headings had not. He trades. He wants the pages that fall from the faded ones, and the fragments of lower writing, and he gives what he kept. A bookmark from him brought me home.
lore.palimpsest.folio.9.title: Folio IX: Below
message.palimpsest.bookbinder.death: The Bookbinder comes apart. Among the pages: a cartographer's spectacles, and a folio.
message.palimpsest.bookbinder.rebind: The Bookbinder draws itself back together. Cut the threads.
message.palimpsest.codex_entry: Your Commonplace Book has a new entry: %s
message.palimpsest.dream.0: You dreamt of a page being turned very slowly.
message.palimpsest.dream.1: You dreamt of lines of writing under the floorboards.
message.palimpsest.dream.2: You dreamt someone was reading over your shoulder.
message.palimpsest.dream.3: You dreamt of a black sun that did not move.
message.palimpsest.dream.4: You dreamt of your own name, scraped off a door.
message.palimpsest.dream.5: You dreamt of knocking. You did not dream of answering.
message.palimpsest.dream_warded: You slept deeply. The red kept watch.
message.palimpsest.ending.read: You read it aloud. The first draft opens around you like a book, and does not close. They can see you now. You can see them.
message.palimpsest.ending.sealed: You write your name over the tear. The ink holds. When you look up, the page is clean, and it is morning.
message.palimpsest.ending.unwritten: You scrape your own name off the page. It comes away easily. Nothing made of ink will ever find you again. Nothing much else will either.
message.palimpsest.first_undertext: The lower writing. The first draft. Everything is quiet the way a page is quiet.
message.palimpsest.folio_stand_empty: The stand is waiting for the last page.
message.palimpsest.gate.disabled: Folio Gates are disabled on this server.
message.palimpsest.gate.incomplete: The frame is not complete: rubricated vellum around an opening two wide and three high.
message.palimpsest.gate.need_night: The Folio will only read after dark.
message.palimpsest.insomnia: You have not slept in days. Something has noticed.
message.palimpsest.lens.scraped: Scraped clean. The words are gone.
message.palimpsest.lens.stone: There is older writing just under the surface.
message.palimpsest.lens.tear: The lower page shows through. It is looking back.
message.palimpsest.no_sleep_undertext: You cannot sleep here. Something is reading over your shoulder.
message.palimpsest.quill.clear: %s writes: and then the rain stopped.
message.palimpsest.quill.morning: %s writes: and then it was morning.
message.palimpsest.quill.nothing: There is nothing here that needs writing.
message.palimpsest.rasure.arrive: The knife has come to finish the page.
message.palimpsest.rasure.death: The Rasure dissolves into pages. On the stand where it stood, the last page of the first draft is waiting.
message.palimpsest.rasure.redaction: It blanks the pillars. Ink them red again.
message.palimpsest.ritual.backlash.bleed: The words are still in your head.
message.palimpsest.ritual.backlash.blotl: The ink runs off the altar.
message.palimpsest.ritual.backlash.fair_: The copy is not the only one.
message.palimpsest.ritual.backlash.knock: Something heard you reading. It is at the door.
message.palimpsest.ritual.backlash.longh: Far off, something tall has turned to face you.
message.palimpsest.ritual.busy: A rite is already being read here.
message.palimpsest.ritual.need_clear: This rite needs a clear sky.
message.palimpsest.ritual.need_day: This rite must be read by daylight.
message.palimpsest.ritual.need_last_foli: This can only be read where the last page is kept.
message.palimpsest.ritual.need_moon_0: This rite must be read under a full moon.
message.palimpsest.ritual.need_moon_4: This rite must be read under a new moon.
message.palimpsest.ritual.need_night: The ink will not take in daylight.
message.palimpsest.ritual.need_overworld: This rite can only be read on the upper page.
message.palimpsest.ritual.need_undertext: This rite can only be read on the lower page.
message.palimpsest.ritual.no_sentence: The offerings do not make a sentence.
message.palimpsest.ritual.not_ready: You have not read enough to read this.
message.palimpsest.rubricator.0: Red does not scrape. Remember that, when it comes.
message.palimpsest.rubricator.1: They took my name. They could not take my headings.
message.palimpsest.rubricator.11: When the birds go quiet, get off the road.
message.palimpsest.rubricator.2: You are the upper writing. You sit on us like frost on a window.
message.palimpsest.rubricator.3: The tall one does not move while you watch. So watch.
message.palimpsest.rubricator.4: Bring me pages. I am putting a book back together.
message.palimpsest.rubricator.5: The cartographer came through here. He bought thread.
message.palimpsest.rubricator.6: Do not open for knocking. Your family has keys.
message.palimpsest.rubricator.7: The knife is not cruel. The knife is only unfinished.
message.palimpsest.rubricator.8: There is a red step outside every house here. Stand on it.
message.palimpsest.rubricator.9: Somewhere above, someone is writing about you right now.
message.palimpsest.rubricator.killed: The last rubricator is gone. The red headings will not be rewritten.
message.palimpsest.sealed_door: It is stitched shut. A key would have to unpick it.
message.palimpsest.sign_undertext.3: SEVEN MILES TO THE RED ROAD
message.palimpsest.sign_undertext.7: THIS WAY TO THE LAST PAGE
message.palimpsest.stage.1: You have the sense you have read this page before.
message.palimpsest.stage.3: The lower writing is coming through.
message.palimpsest.tea.too_soon: Warm, but it does nothing more. Not yet.
palimpsest.configuration.title: Palimpsest
screen.palimpsest.ending.read.desc: Keep the first draft open around you forever. The lower writing will never stop showing through. You wear its crown.
screen.palimpsest.ending.scrape.desc: Take the knife to yourself. What is not written cannot be found.
screen.palimpsest.ending.seal: Write your name over the tear
screen.palimpsest.ending.seal.desc: Close the tear for good. Your page will be clean: no more Bleed, no more visitors. You keep the pen.
screen.palimpsest.ending.text:
Here the first draft ends, mid-sentence. Below the last line, in a hand you know, is the first line of the next page:

%s

The tear is open. The knife is blunt. Something has to be written here.
screen.palimpsest.ending.title: The Last Folio
